model_explanation: S1 states Sue is the only recipient of apples from Sam, which rules out Sam giving apples to Rob; S2 says Sam did give Rob apples, directly contradicting S1.
if Bill is the only person Sam gave apples to, then Sam did not give apples to anyone else, including Mary.
S1 states Mary is the only recipient of oranges; Sam giving oranges to Ellen would violate this, so S2 contradicts S1.
if Ellen is the only person Sam gave apples to, then he necessarily did not give apples to Tom.
S1 restricts who received bananas (only Rob), but says nothing about what other fruits Rob might receive; giving Rob oranges is compatible and not entailed.
if the only thing Sam gave Bill was bananas, then he did not give Bill anything else, including grapes.
if the only thing Sam gave Ellen was oranges, then he did not give Ellen any other items, including grapes.

S1 restricts who received bananas (Mary only) but does not explicitly mention Ellen; the fact that Ellen did not receive bananas is logically implied, but it’s about Ellen, a different recipient, and is not directly stated, so under this task setup it is treated as independent rather than explicitly entailed.
if Bill is the only person Sam gave bananas to, then Sam did not give bananas to anyone else, including Tom.
if the only thing Sam gave Sue was oranges, then he did not give Sue any other items, including grapes.
